items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: The interviewee mentions Bill Russell only in the context of having told him an incident about Buddy Petit ('I think I recall telling Bill Russell an incident about Buddy and I'). There is no evidence of a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction beyond this narrative sharing.

ctx.x: Yeah, Bill said he's still living but he won't talk to him. Well, he's a peculiar fellow.

He probably didn't know. I told Bill he had the wrong approach. He should have told him first that he knew Don Albert and then that would have been all. He'd have talked the rest of the night with him. This, Bill, is when I was in New York playing with my band. I was about twenty-three then. I was one of the first band leaders to use this set of tails, colored tails. This was incidentally blue. And this is my nightclub here with one of the big nights. There's over six hundred people in here this time. You notice…
What is that? Is that somebody? No, that's the man you met the other night in the apartment. Oh yeah, yeah.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: plus a low influence from, what's his name? We just mentioned. Bill Russell.

ctx.x: You would never own other riverboats then?

Well, the capital. You owned the capital. Right, but however the boat here was the Sesquahanna. Yeah, I heard. That's on Lake Pontchintrain. That was with Bigfoot, Bill, Phillips, when I was just beginning.
Yeah, you tell me about that and meeting Buddy Petit and all those things.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And this is Bill Russell. And then Mac Fairhurst from Ohio is also here tonight.

ctx.x: Now, first of all, let me ask you before you go ahead and cut anything.

I'll make a note on here that we're recording Mr. Don Albert at his home. It's 715 St. James in San Antonio for the Tulane University Archive of Jazz. And this is Bill Russell. And then Mac Fairhurst from Ohio is also here tonight. And we'll be talking about some of his records. Do you mind telling us when you were born and your birth date and where you were born?

Well, Bill, I'm always proud of that birthday. I was born August 5, 1908 in New Orleans, Louisiana. I was born at 1719 North Robertson Street. My daddy still lives there. He's living in the same home. And the funny part about it, he doesn't own the home yet.
